requirements.requirement: Provide an operational HTTP forward proxy on node1 TCP port 3128 for use by node2.
requirements.summary: Squid 6.10 was installed from the RHEL repository, configured and enabled on node1. It listened on TCP 3128 before and after node1 restarted, and node2 successfully used it to retrieve the handbook.

requirements.requirement: Permit proxy traffic to the node2 origin on TCP 8081 while rejecting other destination ports, including CONNECT tunnels.
requirements.summary: Direct behavioral tests from node2 returned HTTP 200 for node2:8081, HTTP 403 for port 8080 and another destination, and a 403 CONNECT rejection. The same allow/deny behavior was demonstrated after both nodes restarted and corroborated by Squid's access log.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the staged origin application and make the approved handbook reachable through the proxy from node2.
requirements.summary: Final hashes of serve.py and handbook.txt match the preparation baseline. The enabled origin service listened on node2:8081, served the expected handbook with HTTP 200 through the proxy, and recovered with unchanged content after node2 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained RHEL 10.0 on kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 across execution and restart. Squid 6.10 was obtained from the configured RHEL 10 AppStream repository, and final package-health observations were clean.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service, firewall, data, and end-to-end behavior. The executor boot IDs agree with the fixed after-prepare and after-executor lifecycle observations.
limitations: The final RPM ownership probes for the running kernel returned no matching provider, so package-level kernel ownership was not established. Unchanged running kernel and OS versions are nevertheless directly and consistently shown by the before/after lifecycle observations and executor commands.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node2

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. State-changing commands installed and configured the required proxy, created and corrected the origin unit before enabling it, added narrowly source-restricted persistent firewall rules, enabled the required services, or performed the mandatory restart protocol. The temporary nobody-based service directives were replaced with DynamicUser before activation, while the remainder of that command directly contributed to the final unit. The retained Squid default configuration is a secured rollback copy, not abandoned residue. Both nodes ended with clean package health, no failed services, SELinux enforcing, and only task-required new listeners; restart-created systemd private directories are normal service state.
